accountingMechanism.name: finite source-ledger, not a preset total
accountingMechanism.dateRule: A row cannot move to mapped on a first-flight, launch or contract date. serviceEntry or a documented in-service event is required. modeledAppearance is chosen later and may differ from both.
accountingMechanism.closure: A country-category cell is closed only when every row of each assigned index is in a terminal state and every mapped row cites the evidence that establishes service. Unresolved count is the coverage number. There is no target inventory size.
steps: Register the indexes in sourceIndexes. Add an index before adding a type.
Ingest index rows as unresolved, including names that look familiar.
Normalize license names, NATO names and translations onto one canonical id.
Apply exclusion rules with a quotation, not a memory of the type.
Attach retained operators. A second retained country never creates a second model.
Choose one service configuration for the model. Blocks, marks and sister ships stay on that id.
Only a row in mapped, with geometry still empty, becomes a modelling candidate.
Publish counts as mapped / excluded / ambiguous / unresolved. Never publish a percentage of an imagined complete fleet.
accountingMechanism.whyFinite: Each official or secondary index is finite. The historical problem is that no retained country publishes one official 1914-present type-and-class list. Closure is therefore per index, and the missing historical indexes stay open on purpose.

completenessLimits: Runtime count on 17 November 2026 is 151: 128 surface appearances, 11 aircraft and 12 submarines. Four of the submarines were read from the worktree after the older 8-boat description and were checked against their Navypedia source pages.
147 runtime entries were read from code. They are a sample.
Official pages opened here are current snapshots or anniversary articles. None is a 1914-present type catalogue.
The German equipment book is dated November 2021. The French fleet circular is dated 1 April 2025. They are not silently updated to November 2026.
Wikipedia and Navypedia extracts are reconciliation leads. Their class rows were not accepted as service evidence.

Russia's official English pages confirm categories and a handful of ship names, not classes. China's official articles name some ships and assert submarines without class numbers. Those holes stay open.
US aircraft, pre-1939 US battleships, frigates and auxiliaries, and every country's WWI-to-Cold-War aircraft remain mostly unlisted because their indexes were not ingested.
Empty atlas cells are real. A filled cell is not complete.
No art score is implied by a type being evidenced.
Navypedia fate columns that say in service (2019) are the compiler's freeze date. They are not a 2026 fleet.
